tasks.title: Banner Grabbing & Fingerprinting
tasks.description: Identify the exact OpenSSH version and underlying OS distribution.

tasks.title: Weak Ciphers & Algorithms Check
tasks.description: Enumerate supported algorithms to find deprecated ciphers, which helps troubleshoot connection drops on older targets.

tasks.title: Username Enumeration
tasks.description: Attempt to enumerate valid usernames if older OpenSSH versions (<= 7.7) are in use.

tasks.title: Password Spray (NetExec / CME)
tasks.description: Test weak passwords and custom wordlists against known user accounts.

tasks.title: Hydra Wordlist Brute-Force
tasks.description: Run a targeted brute-force attack against specific users.

tasks.title: Connect via Password or Key
tasks.description: Standard login. Use the -p flag if SSH is on a non-standard port (e.g., 2222). Keys (id_rsa, id_ecdsa, id_dsa) must have 600 permissions.

tasks.title: SCP File Transfers
tasks.description: If you have valid SSH credentials or a key, use SCP to easily push or pull files without needing an external web server.

tasks.title: Fix Malformed Keys
tasks.description: If you are having issues with the formatting of a recovered SSH key, run it through the organization script.

tasks.title: Private Key Cracking
tasks.description: If the discovered private key is encrypted with a passphrase, convert it and crack it using John the Ripper.

tasks.title: Start Local SSH Service
tasks.description: Required before attempting a Reverse Forward (-R). Ensure your Kali SSH daemon is running to catch the incoming connection.

tasks.title: Pivoting: Dynamic Forwarding (-D)
tasks.description:
**The Goal:** Turn your Kali machine into a router for the internal network to use proxychains.

**The Result:** Update `/etc/proxychains4.conf` to `socks5 127.0.0.1 1080`. You can now run `proxychains nmap <Internal_IP>`.

tasks.title: Pivoting: Local Forwarding (-L)
tasks.description:
**The Goal:** Bring a single port from deep inside the network and attach it to your Kali machine (e.g., viewing an internal web server).

**The Result:** Navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:9000` on your Kali browser to see the internal site.

tasks.title: Pivoting: Reverse Forwarding (-R)
tasks.description:
**The Goal:** Send a port from your Kali machine into the compromised network. Critical for catching reverse shells on deeply internal machines.

**How it works:** You log back into your own Kali box from the victim, opening port 60002 on the victim that points back to your Kali listener.
